solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What abused pussy did was greatly appreciated

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme 'Ding Dong Bell', the mistreated cat literally went down the well
a show or idea that ... was well received

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a mistreated cat, followed by praise for something well received.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Ding Dong Bell' begins 'Pussy's in the well', put there by little Johnny Green.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down well is an idiom for being received with approval or enjoyment.

clue.text: Caribbean politicians who lack confidence to act?

definitions.note: a noun-like phrase for people who are feeble, standing for a plural noun

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies, the Caribbean islands
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: A jibe at Caribbean lawmakers too timid to take action.
explanation.walkthrough: WI (West Indies) plus MPS (Members of Parliament) gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimps are feeble, timid people lacking the nerve to take decisive action.

clue.text: Minder of child facing attack — one doesn't offer human milk!

indicators.note: one piece sits facing, i.e. just before, the other in this order

parts.note: a nanny looks after children
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A childminder under attack, with a jokey aside about breastfeeding.
explanation.walkthrough: GO AT (attack) is a two-word phrase here written solid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny goat is a female goat; it gives goat's milk, not human milk, unlike a wet nurse.

clue.text: Making unattractive maiden get out and celebrate

indicators.note: out means the letters of maiden and get are disordered, as in 'put out'

parts.note: to sing can mean to celebrate or praise in song

explanation.surface: Making a young woman less attractive by going out to party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MAIDEN GET into DEMAGNETI, then SING follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Demagnetising removes magnetism, so a magnet no longer attracts iron; literally making something unattractive.

clue.text: Wife is beginning to demand order — that's being prudent

indicators.note: beginning to a word is its first letter, applied here to demand

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A wife insists on things being put in order, calling it sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: OM stands for the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is the quality of sound judgment, so it is the state of being prudent.

clue.text: Thus Barry could become Harry as mindless mistake gets made?

definitions.text: Thus Barry could become Harry as mindless mistake gets made?

parts.words: Thus Barry could become Harry as mindless mistake gets made?
parts.note: changing the first letter of a name gives it the wrong head, and a careless slip is also perverse

explanation.surface: A careless clerk turns Barry into Harry by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Barry and Harry differ only in their initial letter: the name has been given the wrong head.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongheadedly means perversely or in a misguided way, here also literally with the wrong first letter.

clue.text: Policy to omit name in story

indicators.note: to omit something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: A policy that conveniently leaves a name out of the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is a false account, a made-up tale, so it fits as a story.

clue.text: Meals served with hesitation — there's a problem

parts.note: tea is a light evening or afternoon meal in Britain
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Dinners served with someone dithering, which proves troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can be an afternoon or evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a tricky puzzle or brain-teaser, a synonym for a problem.

clue.text: Note small amount drunk

definitions.meaning: a musical note, a half note
a tiny fluid measure, a drop of liquid

explanation.surface: A message about how little someone had to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a minim is the half note; in apothecaries' measure it is about one drop of liquid.

clue.text: European lying in his love-nest

indicators.note: lying in means the word lies concealed inside the following words

explanation.surface: A continental Lothario lounging in his romantic hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying in' shows the answer spanning his lOVE-NEst.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene is a native of Slovenia, a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Keep quiet with yen to be diffident

parts.note: sh is the command to keep quiet
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Advice to stay silent and long for things if timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy and diffident both describe someone reserved and lacking self-confidence.

clue.text: Eurasians who may have lived in the 1700s?

definitions.meaning: People of Georgia, the country straddling Europe and Asia

definitions.text: who may have lived in the 1700s?
definitions.meaning: the Georgian era in Britain covers the reigns of the Georges, mostly the eighteenth century

explanation.surface: People of mixed continental origin, possibly from the eighteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia lies in the Caucasus between Europe and Asia; Britain's four King Georges reigned from 1714 to 1830.

clue.text: But roamer may get confused in this tree garden

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so but roamer is rearranged

explanation.surface: A wanderer might lose their way in this leafy garden.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical collection of trees grown for study and display.

clue.text: "One who avoids work being performed" is about right

indicators.note: is about means one word goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: something performed is done

explanation.surface: A quoted description of a shirker, judged to be about accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee that does no work, hence a lazy idler living off others.

clue.text: Go quietly when external trade is bad

indicators.note: external means one part is outside the other, wrapping around it
bad suggests trade is spoiled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quietly

explanation.surface: Advice to slip away when foreign commerce is going poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges TRADE to DEART, which by 'external' wraps P.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave, a synonym for go.

clue.text: End of Christmas month? One may be glowing

indicators.note: end of means only the tail part of the month's name is kept

parts.note: Christmas falls in December

explanation.surface: Late December, with a fire's remains still glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' keeps the latter part of DECEMBER, dropping DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a smouldering piece of coal or wood that glows in a dying fire.

clue.text: Poet, six, extraordinary girl

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests something out of its usual order, so girl is rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet, aged six, who is a remarkable girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil was the Roman poet who wrote the Aeneid.

clue.text: Being very scared, became very hard

explanation.surface: Someone so frightened they set rigid.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified literally means turned to stone, and figuratively frozen with terror.

clue.text: Little man in fleece

definitions.meaning: A short form of the man's name Robert

explanation.surface: A small fellow wrapped in a woolly fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Rob is a pet form of Robert; to fleece and to rob both mean swindling someone of money.

clue.text: They are tedious drills

explanation.surface: Repetitive exercises that are dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore is a dull person; to bore a hole is to drill it.

clue.text: Unsteady elephant transporter accompanying ruler

indicators.note: accompanying means one piece goes alongside the other, set side by side

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of the Arabian Nights said to carry off elephants
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A wobbly vehicle for an elephant travelling with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc, a mythical giant bird in Sinbad's tales, carries elephants in its claws.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rocking is swaying back and forth, not stable, hence unsteady.

clue.text: Less than completely stylish character in Athens

indicators.note: less than completely means the word is not given in full, losing its final letter

parts.note: chic means stylish

explanation.surface: A not-quite-fashionable figure strolling around the Greek capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less than completely' drops the last C of CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a written character used in Athens.

clue.text: Having resolution halved, being put off

indicators.note: halved means the second half of the word is cut away, leaving its front

parts.note: someone determined has resolution

explanation.surface: Someone's resolve cut in half, so they are discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' drops MINED, the back five of DETERMINED's ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage someone from acting, synonymous with putting them off.

clue.text: Writer's essay — Milking in a New Way

definitions.note: read as Writer is, the definition followed by a link

indicators.note: in a new way means the letters of essay milking are rearranged

explanation.surface: An essay titled as if it were an article on new dairy methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a New Way' rearranges ESSAY MILKING into the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Kingsley Amis was the English novelist who wrote Lucky Jim.
